records.quote:
he had made a mirror with the power of causing all that was good and
      beautiful when it was reflected therein, to look poor and mean; but that
      which was good-for-nothing and looked ugly was shown magnified and
      increased in ugliness
records.paraphrase: A magic mirror is described as distorting reflections so good things look ugly and ugly things look worse.

records.quote:
her hot tears fell just
      where a rose-bush had sunk; and when her warm tears watered the ground,
      the tree shot up suddenly as fresh and blooming as when it had been
      swallowed up
records.paraphrase: Gerda's tears cause a hidden rose-bush to spring up again from the ground.

records.quote:
on she flew with him; flew high over
      the black clouds, while the storm moaned and whistled as though it were
      singing some old tune. On they flew over woods and lakes, over seas, and
      many lands
records.paraphrase: The Snow Queen carries Kay away by flight over great distances of land and sea.

records.quote:
that rose is cankered! And
      look, this one is quite crooked! After all, these roses are very ugly!
records.paraphrase: Kay reacts to the mirror splinter by suddenly seeing beauty as ugliness and becoming cruel.

records.quote:
they penetrated to his heart, they
      thawed the lumps of ice, and consumed the splinters of the looking-glass
records.paraphrase: Gerda's tears melt the ice in Kay's heart and destroy the mirror splinters, reversing his transformation.

records.quote:
There then came a whole regiment of
      snow-flakes, but they did not fall from above, and they were quite bright
      and shining from the Aurora Borealis. The flakes ran along the ground, and
      the nearer they came the larger they grew.
records.paraphrase: Living snowflakes serving as the Snow Queen's outposts move along the ground and grow, taking monstrous shapes.

records.quote:
the splinter rolled
      out of his eye, and he recognised her, and shouted, "Gerda, sweet little
      Gerda! Where have you been so long? And where have I been?"
records.paraphrase: Once the splinter is expelled, Kay weeps, recognizes Gerda, and returns to his former self.

records.quote:
the reason of that is, he has a splinter of glass in his eye, and in his
      heart. These must be got out first; otherwise he will never go back to
      mankind, and the Snow Queen will retain her power over him.
records.paraphrase: The Finland woman explains that Kay's captivity is caused by glass splinters that must be removed to free him.

records.quote:
The cold was so intense that she
      could see her own breath, which came like smoke out of her mouth. It grew
      thicker and thicker, and took the form of little angels
records.paraphrase: Gerda's breath transforms into an army of angels that defend her against the snowflakes.

records.quote:
then he forgot little Gerda, grandmother, and all whom he had left at
      his home
records.paraphrase: After the Snow Queen's kiss, Kay forgets his former life and companions.

records.quote:
The flake of snow grew larger and larger; and at last it was like a young
      lady, dressed in the finest white gauze, made of a million little flakes
      like stars. She was so beautiful and delicate, but she was of ice, of
      dazzling, sparkling ice; yet she lived
records.paraphrase: A snowflake enlarges and becomes the living Snow Queen, a being made of ice.

records.quote:
as they entered, they
      remarked that they were now grown up
records.paraphrase: On returning home, Kay and Gerda find that they have grown up during their long absence.

records.quote:
It was just one of those
      pieces of glass from the magic mirror that had got into his eye; and poor
      Kay had got another piece right in his heart. It will soon become like
      ice.
records.paraphrase: Kay is transformed after mirror fragments enter his eye and heart, foreshadowing his heart turning to ice.

records.quote:
when they got into people's eyes, there
      they stayed; and then people saw everything perverted, or only had an eye
      for that which was evil. This happened because the very smallest bit had
      the same power which the whole mirror had possessed. Some persons even got
      a splinter in their heart, and then it made one shudder, for their heart
      became like a lump of ice.
records.paraphrase: The mirror fragments retain the whole mirror's distorting power and, lodged in eyes or hearts, corrupt people's perception or freeze their feelings.

records.quote:
you can, I know, twist all the
      winds of the world together in a knot. If the seaman loosens one knot,
      then he has a good wind; if a second, then it blows pretty stiffly; if he
      undoes the third and fourth, then it rages so that the forests are
      upturned.
records.paraphrase: The Reindeer describes the Finland woman's power to control winds by binding them in knots that release different wind strengths.

records.quote:
the mirror shook so terribly with grinning, that it flew out of
      their hands and fell to the earth, where it was dashed in a hundred
      million and more pieces
records.paraphrase: The magic mirror shatters into millions of pieces that scatter across the world.

criteria.rationale: The story's 'explanations' (magic mirror, glass splinters freezing hearts, wind-knots) are explicitly magical/fairy-tale mechanics, not scientific facts, theories, natural processes, or speculative sciences. No material scientific representation is present.

The magic mirror is an enchanted/sprite-made object driven by magic, not an engineered device, technique, or invention in any technological sense. It is a supernatural artifact rather than technology or invention.

The tale is a timeless 'once upon a time' fairy setting, not a speculative future or remote past. The children being grown up on return is the passage of ordinary time during a long journey, not temporal displacement or time travel.

The premise that mirror fragments retain the whole mirror's distorting power and, once lodged in eyes/hearts, corrupt perception and freeze feeling is a consequence developed systematically from an established premise. However, the premise is magical rather than scientific/technological/social, so its qualification as extrapolation in the SF sense is uncertain.

No observation, hypothesis, testing, measurement, or evidential revision materially drives understanding or action. Gerda's quest proceeds through faith, tears, and prayer; explanations are pronounced as magical fact, not derived by systematic inference.

The Snow Queen is a living being of ice with a nonordinary icy palace domain, and her animate snowflake outposts constitute a substantially nonordinary environment and visitor from it. This reads as a supernatural/faerie realm rather than another planet or cosmic dimension, so its fit to the criterion is uncertain.

The shattering of the mirror scatters a hundred million+ pieces across the whole world, corrupting people globally, which has a broad malign scale. But it functions as a framing event rather than a depicted large-scale disaster, so its status as a catastrophe is plausible but uncertain.

candidates.description: The wicked sprite's magic mirror that distorts all good and beautiful things into ugliness, then shatters into millions of splinters that lodge in people's eyes and hearts, corrupting perception and freezing feelings.

novelty.rationale: The mirror introduces a world-altering difference from the empirical norm: an object whose fragments scatter globally and systematically pervert human perception and emotion wherever they lodge, changing a crucial aspect of the story universe.

cognitive_validation.rationale: The mirror is the product of a 'wicked sprite' operating on frankly supernatural, magical fairy-tale logic. There is no immanent, systematic, nonsupernatural account (imaginary science or social organization); its power and its reversal (melting via warm tears) are explicitly magical/moral rather than cognitively rationalized.

narrative_hegemony.rationale: The mirror splinters in Kay's eye and heart drive the entire plot: they cause his transformation and abduction, motivate Gerda's quest, and their removal resolves the story. The narrative logic overrides everything else.

estrangement.rationale: The mirror provides a striking reader-facing contrast between ordinary reflection and a device that inverts moral/aesthetic value, with concrete storyworld consequences (Kay's cruelty and abduction) and character reactions (Kay's sudden contempt, later recognition).

candidates.description: The Snow Queen: a living being formed of ice, born from an enlarging snowflake, who flies across lands, abducts Kay, commands living snowflake outposts, and rules an icy palace at the far north.

novelty.rationale: A sentient being made of living ice, capable of flight, memory-erasing kisses, and commanding an army of living snowflakes, is a totalizing departure from empirical norms and reshapes the storyworld.

cognitive_validation.rationale: The Snow Queen is a supernatural fairy-tale personification of winter. Her powers (life from ice, memory-erasing kisses, command over living snow) rest on enchantment, not any immanent, systematic, nonsupernatural logic. This fails Suvin's cognitive requirement.

narrative_hegemony.rationale: The Snow Queen's abduction of Kay and her hold over him structure the whole quest narrative and its resolution.

estrangement.rationale: The transformation of an ordinary snowflake into a living icy queen offers a vivid reader-facing contrast, with storyworld consequences (Kay's abduction and captivity) and character reaction (Kay forgetting his home).

candidates.description: The Finland woman's reputed power to bind all the winds of the world together in a knot, releasing graduated wind strengths as knots are loosened.

novelty.rationale: Control of world winds via knots is unusual, but it is presented as a folk/witchcraft attribution reported by the Reindeer, and its world-altering scope within the story is limited.

cognitive_validation.rationale: This is explicitly witchcraft/magic folk belief, not a systematic nonsupernatural account.

narrative_hegemony.rationale: The wind-knot power is an incidental descriptor of the Finland woman; it does not govern the narrative and is never actually used to change events.

estrangement.rationale: Offers a reader-facing image of graduated wind control, but with no realized storyworld consequences.
